info.title: Servana API — canonical v1
info.description:
The canonical Servana contract. Generated from src/api/v1/contract.ts — do not edit by hand; `npm run api:docs` rewrites it and the contract test fails if it drifts.

Operations marked `x-implemented: false` are DOCUMENTED BUT NOT MOUNTED. They exist so the legacy migration matrix can name a canonical successor before it is built, and they will 404.

Routes under /api/v1 are exempt from the cross-platform field-parity middleware that rewrites every other response, so the shapes below are exactly what the wire carries.

get.summary: The full public catalog tree: categories, their subcategories and their services.
Counts and last-updated stamp for the catalog, for cache validation.
Flat list of every bookable service, for search and deep links.
One service by its canonical services.id, including its place in the hierarchy.
get.description: Deliberately NOT status-filtered: an archived deep link resolves to an honest "unavailable" rather than a 404 dead end. `available` folds in subcategory and category status.

get.summary: The authenticated caller, whatever their role.
The caller's own bookings. Identity comes from the token, never from a parameter.
get.description: Paginated at the API boundary. The underlying service returns the whole set, so this bounds the RESPONSE, not the query — noted in the matrix as a follow-up for the bookings domain command.

get.summary: One booking, if the caller is its customer, its active provider, or an admin.
A booking's operational history, voiced for the customer.
The authenticated provider's job cards.
get.description: Three paths, one domain service. This is the clearest centralization case in the backend: two clients, two shapes, one query.

get.summary: One job card, scoped to the authenticated provider's own assignment.
The caller's notifications.
How many unread notifications the caller has.

patch.summary: Marks one notification read. Repeating it is a no-op, not an error.

post.summary: Marks every notification read. Naturally idempotent.

get.summary: A provider's published reviews. No customer identity is projected.
A provider's aggregate rating.
The caller's notification preferences.
get.description: Three legacy paths, one uid-keyed service, and two of the three are gated on a provider role for a preference table that has no role column. The role gate is the accident, not the capability.

put.summary: Replaces the caller's notification preferences. Idempotent by construction.

post.summary: Creates an account from an email + password, or from a Firebase ID token.
post.description: Registration answers identity only. Provider onboarding, service selection and profile completion are separate domains and are NOT triggered from here beyond the existing non-blocking attribution hooks the legacy path already fires.

post.summary: One sign-in for every identifier and every surface: email or mobile + password, or a Firebase ID token.
post.description: Mobile + password works only for an account that also has an email: Firebase is the password authority and its password grant is keyed on email. An account with a mobile and no email gets PASSWORD_NOT_AVAILABLE and must use the token path — stated, not guessed.

post.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh session.
Ends every session for the authenticated account and clears its push token.
post.description: Ends ALL sessions, not this device only. Firebase has no per-session revocation, and a logout that silently left other devices signed in would be worse than one that says so.

post.summary: Starts password recovery. Always answers the same way, whether or not the account exists.
post.description: EMAIL ONLY today. Recovery requires a VERIFIED identifier, and mobile recovery would need an SMS sender this platform does not have — so it is refused rather than half-built. The response is identical for an unknown address, an unverified one and a mobile number.

post.summary: Completes a password reset and ends every existing session.
Verifies an email address with a one-time code issued for registration.
Re-sends an email verification code or link. Always answers the same way.
Records a mobile number as verified, proven by a Firebase phone credential.
post.description: There is no server-side SMS OTP and this does not add one. The proof is a Firebase ID token whose sign-in provider is `phone`, which Firebase only issues after its own OTP. The number must not already belong to another account — `accountLinkGuard` decides, and a collision is ACCOUNT_LINK_REQUIRED rather than a silent second account.

get.summary: Search Categories, Subcategories and Services in one ranked result set.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. Under 2 characters returns an empty result, not an error.

get.description: Every hit carries a qualified `ref` (`service:180`), so a mixed result set is keyable without the client inferring type from which array it arrived in. Aliases widen what a term MATCHES and never what exists — "aircon" and "air conditioning" return the same Services with the same ids.

get.summary: Alias of /search, scoped under the catalog namespace.
get.description: The command named both paths as the target. Both are mounted and both call the SAME function — two paths, one implementation, which is a naming convenience rather than a second search. If it ever becomes two implementations it is a defect, and tests/v1-catalog-contract.test.ts asserts the shared handler.

get.summary: Lightweight Category summaries with counts, no nested children.
get.description: The counterpart to GET /catalog, which returns the whole tree. A category chooser needing three names should not receive 95 services with prices and images.

get.summary: One Category by canonical catalog_categories.id.
get.description: Not status-filtered: a deep link to a deactivated Category lands on an honest `available: false`.

get.summary: The Subcategories of one Category.
get.description: 404s on a missing Category rather than returning an empty list — empty and missing are different facts.

get.summary: One Subcategory by canonical catalog_subcategories.id.
get.description: `available` folds in the parent Category, as service detail folds in both ancestors.

get.summary: The Services of one Subcategory.
The composed customer home surface.
get.description: No legacy equivalent exists. The customer home surface is assembled on the device from three or four separate calls, so there is nothing to alias — this is a new capability, and building it is a product decision about what home should contain rather than a migration. Listed here so the target architecture is complete.

get.summary: The caller's booking conversations.
The authenticated provider's earnings summary.
get.description: Money. Deliberately not adapted in a foundation command: the payout window is already documented as 48h in copy and 72h in reality, and a second read path before that is settled would give two answers to "when am I paid".

get.summary: The canonical transition history: one event per state change, oldest first.
get.description: Preserves a reassigned provider's full progression — accepted, en route, reassigned — because the current state resetting must not erase history.

post.summary: Declines the assignment, returning the booking to the pool.
Marks the provider on the way.
Marks the provider at the address.
Starts the job. Requires the customer worker code.
post.description: The worker code is the six-digit secret the CUSTOMER reads out. It is the only gate on starting a chargeable job, so it is rate-limited per provider and is redacted before the timeline records the transition.

get.summary: Admin booking operations list.

firebaseIdToken.description: Verified signature AND revocation state — a token issued before a session revocation is rejected with TOKEN_REVOKED, not accepted until expiry.

message.description: Human-readable. Never branch on this — branch on `code`.

details.description: Optional structured context. Shape depends on `code`.

requestId.description: Also returned as the X-Request-Id header.

total.description: null when the total is not cheaply knowable.

lastUpdatedAt.description: ISO 8601 with a UTC designator. Never Postgres' native "2026-08-11 11:03:23.421016+00".

CatalogRef.description: Qualified canonical reference, e.g. `service:180`. Four different things in this platform are called a "service id" — services.id, service_families.id, service_options.id and a subcategory id — and three are integers in overlapping ranges. A ref cannot be read as the wrong one. Prefer it as a cache key and for cross-entity result sets; `id` remains authoritative for path parameters.

CatalogService.description: Never carries `level2`/`level_2`. In the legacy model those mean the SUBCATEGORY; response parity used to map `name` onto them, which made a Service claim its own name as its subcategory. /api/v1 is exempt from that middleware.

available.description: Folds in subcategory and category status. Detail is NOT status-filtered, so an archived deep link resolves to an honest "unavailable" rather than a 404.

CategorySummary.description: No nested children. Use /catalog/categories/{id}/subcategories for the next level.

available.description: Detail is NOT status-filtered, so a deep link to a deactivated Category resolves honestly.
Folds in the parent Category status.

id.description: Canonical id WITHIN its type. Read `ref` to key across types.

bookable.description: Services only. A Category cannot be booked.

matchedTerm.description: The query, or the alias that widened it. Makes a surprising hit explainable.

expandedTerms.description: Every term the query was widened to via the alias table.

SearchResults.description: Aliases widen what a term MATCHES, never what exists. "aircon" and "air conditioning" return the same Services with the same ids.

expectedState.description: Optimistic concurrency. Send the state you last read and get a clean BOOKING_STATE_CONFLICT instead of silently acting on a stale view.

reason.description: Required by cancellation and reassignment guards.

workerCode.description: Six digits the CUSTOMER reads out. Required to start a job. Redacted before the timeline.

BookingActionRequest.description: Send Idempotency-Key as a HEADER; a retry replays the original result.

idempotentReplay.description: True when an identical request had already been applied.

state.description: The caller-appropriate projection of the new state.

BookingTransitionList.description: Append-only. A reassigned provider keeps their progression — the current state resetting must not erase what happened.

id.description: Same value as uid. Present for clients that key on `id`.

uid.description: The Firebase uid. THE primary key — there is no numeric user id.

role.description: 1 admin, 2 and 4 provider, 3 customer. See servana_role_map.

Booking.description: A booking as produced by bookingService.formatBooking.

BookingTimeline.description: Operational history, voiced for the customer. Not the audit record (§16).

JobCard.description: A job card as produced by controllers/jobCardView.formatJobCard.

NotificationMutation.description: Outcome flags from the notification service.

NotificationPreferences.description: Per-channel preference flags, keyed by uid.

token.description: Firebase ID token. Lives ONE HOUR — refresh before it expires.

refreshToken.description: Long-lived. Belongs in secure device storage, never a log or a query string. Exchange it at POST /api/v1/auth/refresh.

uid.description: The Firebase uid. THE primary key — there is no numeric user id.

identifierType.description: Which identifier the caller actually presented.

identifier.description: Email address OR Philippine mobile number, in any form a person types (0917…, +63917…, 9171234567). Required with `password`.

idToken.description: Firebase ID token. Alternative to identifier+password.

audience.description: Which surface is asking. Asserted AFTER authentication, so the admin login box is not an oracle for "is this address an admin". Defaults to `any`.

role.description: Token path only: role a NEW account is created with.

fcmToken.description: Optional. Registered non-blocking; failure never fails the sign-in.

role.description: 2 provider or 3 customer. Admin accounts cannot be created here.

platform.description: Governs whether verification is a code or a link.

verificationDeliveryPending.description: The account exists but the code or link did not go out. Not a failure — retry delivery via resend-verification rather than re-registering, which would collide with the identity.

identifier.description: Email address. Mobile recovery is not configured — see the contract.

platform.description: Allowlisted name, never a URL. Chooses where the link lands.

oobCode.description: Single-use code from the reset email.

platform.description: Link channel only. Allowlisted name, never a URL.

idToken.description: A Firebase ID token whose sign-in provider is `phone`, or which has a phone credential linked. Firebase only issues one after its own SMS OTP.

LogoutResult.description: Ends ALL sessions — Firebase has no per-session revocation.

NeutralAck.description: Deliberately identical whether or not the account exists. The difference between "that address is not registered" and "sent" is a free membership check.

ConversationList.description: PLANNED — owned by the messaging domain command.

EarningsSummary.description: PLANNED — owned by the provider-earnings domain command.

AdminBookingList.description: PLANNED — owned by the admin-bookings domain command.
